titleBlock.headline: How Declining Endogenous Metabolites Influence Aging and What Replenishment Can Achieve

researchSummary:
This is a summary of the scientific study.
Not affiliated with the study authors or their institutions.
whatIsClock: They are naturally occurring small molecules—intermediates of the TCA cycle, amino acid metabolism, polyamines, and ketone bodies—whose intracellular and circulating levels decline with age and directly govern cellular homeostasis.

Unlike synthetic xenobiotics, endogenous metabolites act as native cofactors for chromatin-modifying enzymes (such as sirtuins and TET/JMJD demethylases) and allosteric regulators of nutrient-sensing hubs (AMPK, mTOR, IIS, FOXO).

This 2026 Aging Cell review synthesizes cross-species evidence across C. elegans, Drosophila, mice, and human trials for 9 core endogenous metabolites—distinguishing those with proven mammalian lifespan extension (AKG, Taurine, Spermidine) from those with invertebrate lifespan and mammalian healthspan evidence.

studyOverview.label: Objective
studyOverview.value: Synthesize mechanisms, cross-species lifespan data, and clinical translation challenges of declining endogenous longevity metabolites.

studyOverview.label: Design
studyOverview.value: Systems-biology review of 9 endogenous metabolites across nutrient-sensing, epigenetic, and mitophagy networks.

studyOverview.label: Scope
studyOverview.value: C. elegans, Drosophila, murine lifespan/healthspan cohorts, and human clinical/epidemiological studies.

studyOverview.label: Key Focus
studyOverview.value: Cofactor roles in TET/JMJD/Sirtuin epigenetics, AMPK/mTOR/FOXO signaling, and mitochondrial quality control.

scorecardOverview.title: The Question
scorecardOverview.content: Why do specific endogenous metabolites systematically decline during aging—and to what extent can replenishing them extend lifespan or restore tissue function in mammals and humans?

scorecardOverview.title: The Methodology
scorecardOverview.content: Comprehensive cross-species synthesis (C. elegans, Drosophila, mice, non-human primates, and human trials) mapping 9 endogenous metabolites onto the hallmarks of aging and nutrient-sensing/epigenetic pathways.

scorecardOverview.title: The Breakthrough
scorecardOverview.content: Clarifies the translational hierarchy: Ca-AKG, Taurine, and Spermidine extend both lifespan and healthspan in mice, whereas NAD+ precursors, BHB, OAA, Betaine, Myo-inositol, and H2S show invertebrate lifespan extension and potent mammalian healthspan rejuvenation.

mechanismDescription: Endogenous metabolites serve as direct physical links between metabolic flux and the epigenome—acting as obligate cosubstrates (e.g., NAD+ for Sirtuins/PARPs, AKG for TET/JMJD demethylases, SAM/Betaine for methyltransferases) and allosteric switches for AMPK, mTOR, and FOXO.
translationalChallenges: Species gap in lifespan proof: While Ca-AKG (Asadi Shahmirzadi et al., 2020), Taurine (Singh et al., 2023), and Spermidine (Eisenberg et al., 2016) extend both lifespan and healthspan in mice, other metabolites (OAA, H2S, Myo-inositol, Trehalose) currently have lifespan proof only in invertebrates, and human clinical trials remain limited to healthspan and biomarker endpoints.

Context-dependent pleiotropy & biomarker controversies: For example, while Taurine supplementation extended mouse lifespan by 10–12% (Singh et al., 2023), longitudinal human cohort analyses (Fernandez et al., 2025) revealed complex age- and context-dependent trajectories of circulating taurine.

Bioavailability, tissue targeting, and dosing windows: Endogenous metabolites undergo rapid gut/hepatic clearance and feedback regulation, requiring optimized precursor selection (e.g., Ca-AKG sustained-release, NMN/NR) and precision dosing.

keyFindings.title: Multi-Pathway Network Modulators
keyFindings.desc: Endogenous metabolites simultaneously modulate AMPK activation, mTORC1 restraint, autophagy/mitophagy, and redox balance—avoiding the single-pathway escape common to synthetic drugs.

keyFindings.title: Direct Epigenetic Cosubstrates
keyFindings.desc: AKG serves as the obligate cofactor for TET DNA demethylases and JMJD histone demethylases, NAD+ powers Sirtuin deacetylases, BHB inhibits HDACs, and Betaine supplies SAM for methylation.

keyFindings.title: Mammalian Lifespan vs. Healthspan Hierarchy
keyFindings.desc: Ca-AKG (+12% median lifespan and -46% frailty in female mice), Taurine (+10–12% mouse lifespan), and Spermidine (+10% late-life mouse survival) lead mammalian longevity evidence.

keyFindings.title: Evolutionary Conservation
keyFindings.desc: Pathways linking TCA intermediates (AKG, OAA), polyamines (Spermidine), and sulfur amino acids (Taurine, H2S) to stress resistance are conserved from nematodes to mammals.

findingsCallout: By acting as direct allosteric modulators and enzymatic cosubstrates, endogenous metabolites physically link the cell's bioenergetic state to its chromatin architecture and lifespan-regulating transcriptional programs.
keyTakeaway: Replenishing age-depleted endogenous metabolites offers a biocompatible, multi-hallmark strategy to restore youthful epigenetic and nutrient-sensing states—with Ca-AKG, Taurine, and Spermidine demonstrating both lifespan and healthspan extension in mice.
protocolRecommendations: Prioritize multi-pathway metabolic replenishment (combining TCA/epigenetic cofactors like Ca-AKG with NAD+ precursors or autophagy inducers like Spermidine) rather than relying on isolated single-target compounds.
Match metabolite selection to validated biological endpoints: use Ca-AKG, Taurine, and NAD+ precursors to support mitochondrial OXPHOS, epigenetic maintenance, and inflammatory restraint.
Pair endogenous supplementation with exercise and fasting/circadian nutrition, which naturally elevate endogenous BHB, AKG, NAD+/NADH ratios, and spermidine-driven autophagy.

topMetabolites.name: α-Ketoglutarate (Ca-AKG)
topMetabolites.mechanism: Inhibits ATP synthase/mTOR, activates AMPK, and serves as obligate cofactor for TET DNA & JMJD histone demethylases.
topMetabolites.effect: Extends C. elegans lifespan by ~50% (Chin et al., 2014) and female mouse median lifespan by ~12% while compressing morbidity/frailty by >40% (Asadi Shahmirzadi et al., 2020).

topMetabolites.name: Taurine
topMetabolites.mechanism: Supports mitochondrial tRNA taurine modification (5-taurinomethyluridine), Electron Transport Chain complex I, redox balance, and reduces senescence/DNA damage.
topMetabolites.effect: Daily supplementation extended mouse median lifespan by 10–12% and improved bone, muscle, brain, and immune healthspan in mice and monkeys (Singh et al., 2023; human biomarker nuances noted in Fernandez et al., 2025).

topMetabolites.name: Spermidine
topMetabolites.mechanism: Inhibits EP300 acetyltransferase and drives eIF5A hypusination/TFEB translation to induce autophagy and PINK1/Parkin mitophagy.
topMetabolites.effect: Extends lifespan across yeast, flies, worms, and mice (~10% late-life extension), reversing age-related cardiac hypertrophy and preserving diastolic function (Eisenberg et al., 2016).

topMetabolites.name: NAD+ Precursors (NR / NMN)
topMetabolites.mechanism: Replenishes nuclear and mitochondrial NAD+ pools to activate Sirtuins (SIRT1/SIRT3) and PARPs, reversing HIF-1α pseudohypoxia.
topMetabolites.effect: Restores youthful mitochondrial OXPHOS, vascular capillarity, and insulin sensitivity in aged mice; NR extended late-life mouse lifespan in Zhang et al. (2016), while ITP showed sex/dose nuances.

topMetabolites.name: β-Hydroxybutyrate (BHB)
topMetabolites.mechanism: Endogenous ketone body that inhibits Class I HDACs, suppresses the NLRP3 inflammasome, and activates FOXO3a/Nrf2 antioxidant signaling.
topMetabolites.effect: Extends C. elegans lifespan by ~20% and in aged mice preserves mid-life survival, memory, and muscle mitochondrial function via ketogenic/ester protocols (Roberts et al., 2017).

topMetabolites.name: Betaine (Trimethylglycine)
topMetabolites.mechanism: One-carbon methyl donor that regenerates methionine and S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), lowering homocysteine and activating AMPK.
topMetabolites.effect: Extends C. elegans lifespan and in aged mice attenuates inflammaging, hepatic steatosis, and skeletal muscle wasting; Identified as an exercise-induced renal mimetic.

topMetabolites.name: Oxaloacetate (OAA)
topMetabolites.mechanism: TCA cycle intermediate whose cytosolic reduction to malate increases the NAD+/NADH ratio, activating AMPK and FOXO/DAF-16.
topMetabolites.effect: Extends C. elegans lifespan by ~25% (Williams et al., 2009) and improves brain bioenergetics and neurogenesis markers in preclinical rodent studies.

topMetabolites.name: Myo-Inositol & Trehalose
topMetabolites.mechanism: Myo-inositol regulates PI3K/AKT/IIS and PTEN mitophagy; Trehalose acts as an mTOR-independent TFEB autophagy activator and chemical chaperone.
topMetabolites.effect: Both extend C. elegans lifespan (>30%) and protect against proteotoxic aggregation and metabolic insulin resistance in mammalian tissues.

topMetabolites.name: Hydrogen Sulfide (H2S)
topMetabolites.mechanism: Endogenous gasotransmitter (via CBS/CSE/3-MST) mediating protein persulfidation (S-sulfhydration), SIRT1 stabilization, and mitochondrial bioenergetics.
topMetabolites.effect: Required for dietary restriction-mediated longevity across species; extends C. elegans lifespan up to 70% and protects aged mammalian vasculature.

conclusions: Endogenous metabolites are native, multi-target modulators of longevity that physically couple cellular energy status to epigenetic maintenance.

Ca-AKG, Taurine, and Spermidine have demonstrated both lifespan and healthspan extension in mice, while NAD+ precursors, BHB, Betaine, OAA, Myo-inositol, and H2S show strong cross-species healthspan and mechanistic support.
Clinical translation to humans requires rigorous dose optimization, sustained-release formulations, and longitudinal biomarker validation.

structuredConclusions.title: Metabolism Directly Writes the Epigenome
structuredConclusions.content: Age-related depletion of AKG, NAD+, BHB, and SAM/Betaine directly starves TET/JMJD demethylases, Sirtuins, and methyltransferases—meaning metabolic replenishment is required to sustain youthful gene expression.

structuredConclusions.title: Evidence Stratification Across Species
structuredConclusions.content: While all 9 metabolites extend invertebrate lifespan, Ca-AKG (+12% female lifespan, -46% frailty), Taurine (+10–12% lifespan), and Spermidine (+10% survival) have established mammalian lifespan extension in mice.

structuredConclusions.title: Precision Dosing & Biomarker Nuances
structuredConclusions.content: Human translation requires accounting for rapid pharmacokinetics, sex-specific responses, and longitudinal biomarker dynamics (such as context-dependent human taurine trajectories).
